# No selector based only on the individual fiber can prove OC

Consider any deterministic rule assigning one point p_z(K) in every planar
convex body K, for each integer index z. The rule may depend on z and on the
fixed dimensions n=1,d=2, but not on the other fibers. The proposed global
method is allowed to choose whichever of these per-fiber points is best.
There is no such rule that succeeds for every mixed-integer convex body.

Proof. Let T be the standard triangle, with centroid g. Its unique point of
depth at least gamma_2=4/9 is g: for any other point, some barycentric
coordinate exceeds 1/3, and the corresponding vertex cap has relative area
strictly less than 4/9.

For each integer a, the body [a,a+1] x T has exactly its two endpoint
integer fibers. A containing ambient halfspace can isolate either fiber
and realize any prescribed cap there. Consequently its points of depth at
least 2/9 are precisely (a,g) and (a+1,g). If the proposed rule succeeds
on all these products, there is at least one integer k with p_k(T)=g.
(In fact such k must meet every adjacent pair of integer indices.)

Now let B=T intersect {x<=1/3}, with area(B)=5 area(T)/9, and take

  C=conv(({k-1} x B) union ({k} x T) union ({k+1} x B)).

Its three fibers are exactly B,T,B. Total mixed area is19 area(T)/9.
At the selected middle point (k,g), the halfspace x>=1/3 has normalized
mass4/19<2/9. Every point in either endpoint fiber has depth at most
5/38<2/9: choose one of two complementary through-point planar halfspaces
having at most half that fiber's area, and add a sufficiently large
integer-coordinate coefficient to exclude both other fibers.

Thus all three points selected by the rule fail. This argument does not
restrict their positions in B, and establishes the impossibility claimed.

In particular, replacing each fiber centroid by its intrinsic deepest
point cannot repair the centroid-only route. Any successful construction
must use the geometry of other fibers when selecting a point in a given
fiber, or retain more than one context-free candidate there.
